cards.explanation: The answer is to write them in a book. The LORD tells Jeremiah, "Write in a book all the words that I have spoken to you." (Jeremiah 30:2) Not some of them, not the highlights, ALL of them. Jeremiah, the prophet who spoke for the LORD, gets a big writing assignment, friends.

The answer is that He will restore them from captivity. The LORD says, "…I will restore from captivity My people Israel and Judah…" (Jeremiah 30:3) Captivity is not where their story ends, friends. When He says the days are coming, He's talking about a way home.

The word is "possess." The LORD says He will restore them to the land He gave their fathers, "…and they will possess it." (Jeremiah 30:3) Possess means it's theirs again. They're not just stopping by to look around, bakers.
The word is "pale." The LORD says He sees "…every face turned pale?" (Jeremiah 30:6) Picture everyone's color just draining out at once, friends. That's what real terror looks like.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "It is the time of Jacob’s distress, but he will be saved out of it." (Jeremiah 30:7) Notice the "but," friends. The day is awful, and Jacob still comes out the other side.

The answer is that no more strangers will enslave them. The LORD says, "…I will break the yoke off their necks and tear off their bonds, and no longer will strangers enslave them." (Jeremiah 30:8) Look at what comes right after, friends. They go from being enslaved to serving the LORD their God (Jeremiah 30:9).

The answer is the LORD their God and their king. The LORD says, "…they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them." (Jeremiah 30:9) They stop serving strangers and start serving the One who is actually theirs, bakers. That's a trade I'd make any day.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "As for you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid… For I will surely save you out of a distant place…" (Jeremiah 30:10) He calls Jacob His servant right in the middle of the fear, friends. That's a good way to be talked to.

The answer is quiet and ease. The LORD says, "Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid." (Jeremiah 30:10) Quiet, ease and nobody making him afraid, bakers. That sounds like a kitchen after the last batch is out and the dishes are done.

The answer is that He will not completely destroy His own people. The LORD says, "Though I will completely destroy all the nations to which I have scattered you, I will not completely destroy you." (Jeremiah 30:11) He's with them to save them, and He says so right there, friends. Their story keeps going.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…I am with you to save you…" and then adds, "Yet I will discipline you justly, and will by no means leave you unpunished." (Jeremiah 30:11) Both are true at once, friends. He saves them, and He doesn't let it go unpunished.

The answer is that they have forgotten them. The LORD says, "All your lovers have forgotten you; they no longer seek you…" (Jeremiah 30:14) Nobody pleads their cause, and the lovers no longer seek them. I think that's a lonely spot, friends.

The answer is True, and it's a heavy one. The LORD says, "…I have struck you as an enemy would, with the discipline of someone cruel, because of your great iniquity and your numerous sins." (Jeremiah 30:14) He gives the reason right in the verse, friends. This part is hard, so I'll just say it plainly and let it sit.

The answer is that the same thing happens to them. The LORD says, "all who devour you will be devoured… Those who plundered you will be plundered, and all who raided you will be raided." (Jeremiah 30:16) What they did comes back around to them, bakers. And that "nevertheless" is where the whole thing turns.

The answer is True. The wound has no cure, and then comes the LORD: "…I will restore your health and heal your wounds, declares the LORD…" (Jeremiah 30:17) No cure, and He heals anyway, friends. Don't miss that.

The reason is that they call her an outcast no one cares for. The LORD says, "…I will restore your health and heal your wounds, declares the LORD, because they call you an outcast, Zion, for whom no one cares." (Jeremiah 30:17) Zion is Jerusalem, bakers. Others called her uncared for, and He steps in anyway.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…the city will be rebuilt on her own ruins, and the palace will stand in its rightful place." (Jeremiah 30:18) The ruins are the starting spot, friends, and the palace goes right where it belongs. It's a rebuild.

The word is "celebration." The LORD says, "Thanksgiving will proceed from them, a sound of celebration." (Jeremiah 30:19) Remember that cry of terror from earlier, friends? Now it's a different sound coming out of them.

The answer is that he comes from among their own. The LORD says, "Their leader will be one of their own, and their ruler will arise from their midst." (Jeremiah 30:21) He comes from their own people, friends. Nobody has to bring in an outsider.

The word is "wicked." "Behold, the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked." (Jeremiah 30:23) The verse names who the whirlwind falls on, bakers. I think this is a heavy verse, and it's worth reading slowly.

The answer is False. The verse says, "The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart." (Jeremiah 30:24) So the anger does not turn back before the job is done, friends. Then the verse ends with this: "In the days to come you will understand this."

The answer is all the families of Israel. The LORD says, "I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be My people." (Jeremiah 31:1) Notice the word all, friends. Every family is in.
